paintings.title: The Starry Night
paintings.description: Painted during Van Gogh's stay at Saint-Rémy, this swirling night sky captures the artist's turbulent inner world — a visual echo of the moon theme's contemplation of light in darkness.

paintings.title: Sunflowers
paintings.description: A celebration of life and decay in equal measure. These sunflowers, painted in Arles, embody the sunflower theme — turning toward light even as they wilt.

paintings.title: Wheatfield with Crows
paintings.description: One of Van Gogh's final paintings, this turbulent wheat field under a stormy sky speaks to the ego theme — the struggle between the self and the vast, indifferent universe.

paintings.title: The Night Café
paintings.description: Van Gogh described this as 'a place where one can ruin oneself, go mad, or commit a crime.' The harsh reds and greens embody the Gita's warning about the destructive power of unchecked desire.

paintings.title: Self-Portrait
paintings.description: Painted after his hospitalization, this self-portrait reveals the artist's inner storm. The swirling background echoes the Shiva theme — destruction and creation intertwined in the dance of existence.

paintings.title: Irises
paintings.description: Painted in the asylum at Saint-Rémy, these irises pulse with life. Each flower is unique — a meditation on the art theme's celebration of beauty in impermanence.

paintings.title: Café Terrace at Night
paintings.description: The first painting where Van Gogh used a starry night sky. The warm yellow café against the cool blue night captures the moon theme's duality — human warmth against cosmic vastness.

paintings.title: Almond Blossom
paintings.description: Painted to celebrate the birth of his nephew, this luminous work embodies the Gita's teaching of selfless joy — new life as an offering, not a possession.
